correctness.rationale: An exact 16-equation stationary Pauli-string system yields the displayed four-site resistance. Reconstructing the two- and three-site currents checks the normalization. For nonzero tilt, exact integer polynomial expansion gives 85 strictly positive coefficients in the numerator making the field resistance decreasing, and 224 strictly positive coefficients in its second-derivative numerator, proving strict convexity over all positive bath couplings and nonnegative dephasing. The zero-dephasing derivative has the exact stated polynomial with strictly positive nonconstant coefficients and a negative constant, so exactly one positive field threshold exists. Limiting derivative 3/8 proves the full global optimizer dichotomy; dominant balances prove both coupling-limit constants. The embedded checker establishes these exact identities and independently compares 150 direct covariance systems. Numerical samples are not used as proofs.

value.rationale: A natural finite four-site model is the first chain length beyond the motivating paper’s explicit exact results. The new full-parameter theorem rules out multiple dephasing optima for the uniform-gradient current, gives a sharp design inequality rather than only numerical optima, and discovers a singular weak/strong reservoir-coupling disappearance of the onset threshold. That structural distinction matters because other dephased potential landscapes can have two resonances. No general theorem for larger chains or paper-sized downstream application is claimed.
